metaDescription: Six wood lathes from 12 x 21 midi to 18 x 40 full size, compared on swing, bed length, motor, speed range and headstock design for bowls and spindles.
expertTake: The JET JWL-1640EVS is the best pick for a turner who wants a full-size, electronically variable lathe that grows with them. The WEN 34035 is the value pick for a first lathe that handles bowls and spindles on a budget. Anyone who only turns pens and small items should read the mini lathe guide instead, because these machines are bigger than they need.
introParagraphs: A wood lathe spins a blank of wood while you shape it with hand-held tools. It is the machine behind bowls, spindles, table legs, pens and bats, and it rewards patience more than strength. The difference between a pleasant lathe and a frustrating one is mass, speed control and how well the headstock handles an out-of-balance blank.

Two numbers define the size: swing, the largest diameter that clears the bed, and the distance between centres, the longest piece you can mount. After that, the motor, the speed range and the build material decide how the machine behaves with a large rough blank spinning at the start.

products.name: JET JWL-1640EVS 16 x 40 in EVS Lathe, 1-1/2HP Reversible
products.description:
The JWL-1640EVS is a full-size lathe with 16 inches of swing and 40 inches between centres, powered by a 1-1/2 HP motor on 115V with electronic infinitely variable speed from 40 to 3,200 RPM. It is reversible, which helps with sanding, and the listing mentions an extended spindle nose housing dual headstock bearings.

The 40 RPM floor is the key number. Large, rough blanks are dangerous at high speed, and being able to start at a crawl and creep up lets you turn a big out-of-balance bowl blank safely. The 16 inch swing handles most bowls, and 40 inches between centres covers table legs and spindles. Compared with the JET 1221VS at 60 to 3,600, it has more swing and a lower minimum.

It is heavy, which is a feature, since mass damps vibration. Expect to spend on a chuck, faceplates and tools separately. It is a lathe you can keep for decades. Plan for a heavy stand or bench, because a machine this size is only as steady as what it sits on.
products.bestFor: Turners who want a full-size lathe with a very low minimum speed.
cons: Heavy and takes real bench or stand space
Higher price tier than hobby lathes

products.name: Laguna Revo 18|36 Wood Lathe 1.5HP VFD Reversible
products.description:
The Revo 18|36 offers 18 inches of swing and 36 inches of capacity, a 1.5 HP TEFC induction motor on 110V and a Delta S1 variable frequency drive. A sliding headstock lets you move the work along the bed, and the controls are positioned ergonomically.

An induction motor with a VFD is the modern route to quiet, strong, infinitely variable speed. It gives good torque at low speed and runs cooler than a brushed motor. The sliding headstock is useful for turning large bowls: you can slide the headstock to give clearance beyond the bed end. Compared with the JET 1640EVS, it has two more inches of swing at a slightly shorter bed.

The cost is the top price tier in the guide. It is a serious machine for turners who work on large bowls and platters. Budget for a chuck and good tools. Sliding the headstock out and turning outboard is a trick worth practising early, because it opens the size range without buying a bigger bed.
products.bestFor: Turners of large bowls and platters who want a sliding headstock.
cons: Bed is 36 in, shorter than 40 in rivals

products.name: JET JWL-1440VS 14 x 40 in Variable Speed, 1HP 115/230V
products.description:
The JWL-1440VS has a sliding headstock that pivots 360 degrees with seven locking positions, 0 to 270 degrees, and a variable speed range of 400 to 3,000 RPM from a 1 HP motor that runs on 115V or 230V. The 14 by 40 inch capacity is mid-size.

A pivoting headstock lets you turn the work out over the bed end, so you can turn a bowl larger than the bed swing allows by rotating the headstock and standing in front of the work. The 400 RPM minimum is higher than the EVS models, so starting a large blank safely means using belt ranges carefully. Compared with the JET 1640EVS, it has less swing and a higher minimum speed.

A 1 HP motor is adequate for most bowls up to about 12 inches. It is a good middle lathe for a home shop. Use the lowest speed that gives a clean cut when roughing, then climb through the range as the blank comes into round.
products.bestFor: Home turners who want pivoting-headstock flexibility at mid size.
cons: 400 RPM minimum is high for big blanks

products.name: VEVOR 2HP Wood Lathe 18 x 40 in, Brushless DC
products.description:
The VEVOR 2HP offers 18 by 40 inch capacity with a 2 HP, 1500W brushless DC motor and a 150 to 3,200 RPM variable speed range, on a cast iron body. A brushless DC motor gives smooth torque and strong low-speed behaviour. The listing describes a vertical lathe design.

On paper it matches the Laguna in swing with more horsepower at a much lower price tier. The difference is in the details you cannot see in a spec sheet: bearing quality, spindle runout, tool-rest finish and long-term support. A 150 RPM minimum is higher than the JET's 40 but workable with care.

If you want big capacity on a budget and are willing to tune the machine, it is attractive. Check the spindle thread, and budget for a chuck. It is a bargain for the right buyer. Check the spindle thread and Morse taper size before ordering any chuck, since a mismatch is a common first-month mistake.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want 18 in swing and strong motor power.
cons: Brand support is thin for a large lathe
150 RPM minimum is higher than premium units

products.name: JET JWL-1221VS 12 x 21 in Variable Speed, 1HP

specList.label: Build
specList.value: Cast iron bed and tool support

products.description:
The JWL-1221VS is the midi-lathe benchmark, 12 inches of swing and 21 inches between centres with a 1 HP motor and three belt ranges from 60 to 3,600 RPM. The bed, tool support and base are cast iron.

A midi lathe is the sweet spot for most hobby turners: it handles bowls up to about 10 inches, spindles up to 21 inches and pens and small items with ease. The 60 RPM low end is excellent for a lathe this size, though you must change the belt to switch ranges. Compared with the WEN 34035, it is better built and more expensive.

It sits on a bench or its own stand. Expect to buy a chuck and tools. It is a good first serious lathe. Keep the belt guard closed, and replace the belt at the first sign of glazing.
products.bestFor: Hobby turners who want a well-built midi lathe for bowls and spindles.
pros: 60 to 3,600 RPM in three belt ranges
cons: Belt changes to switch speed ranges

products.name: WEN 34035 14 x 20 in Variable Speed Benchtop Lathe
products.description:
The WEN 34035 has a 14 inch swing and 20 inch bed, a 6 amp motor and a variable speed range from 250 to 3,550 RPM. It is the cheapest lathe here by priceTier and aimed at beginners.

The 14 inch swing is generous for a benchtop lathe, which lets you try larger bowls than a mini lathe permits. The 6 amp motor is modest, so a large blank will stall it at low speed, and its 250 RPM minimum is higher than the premium lathes. Compared with the JET 1221VS, it has more swing but less mass and refinement.

It is a good first lathe if you take light cuts and keep blanks small and balanced. Bolt it to a heavy bench to damp vibration. Add a ballast of sandbags to a lightweight stand, and bolt the lathe down so it cannot walk.
products.bestFor: Beginners who want the largest swing at the lowest price tier.
cons: 6 amp motor stalls on large blanks

buyingCriteria.explanation: Swing is the largest diameter you can turn over the bed, and distance between centres is the longest spindle. A midi lathe like the JET JWL-1221VS at 12 x 21 handles bowls to about 10 inches. A full-size lathe like the JET 1640EVS at 16 x 40 handles table legs and large bowls. Buy for the largest piece you expect to turn regularly. If you are unsure, buy slightly more swing than you think you need, because nobody regrets the extra capacity.

A large blank is unbalanced and must be started slowly. The JET 1640EVS starts at 40 RPM and the JET 1221VS at 60, while the WEN 34035 starts at 250 RPM and the JET 1440VS at 400. Higher minimums limit how big a blank you can safely start, so check the number against your plans. Start every rough blank at the lowest speed and step up only after it runs smoothly.

Electronic variable speed with a VFD or brushless DC motor, as on the Laguna Revo, JET 1640EVS and VEVOR 2HP, gives good torque at low speed and avoids belt changes. Belt-driven systems like the JET 1221VS need manual belt moves to change ranges but are simple and durable. Torque at low speed matters more than peak horsepower. A heavier motor with strong low-speed torque is the best defence against catches in a bowl.

A heavy cast iron bed damps the vibration caused by an unbalanced blank. Lightweight benchtop lathes like the WEN 34035 need a heavy bench and sandbags to behave. If you plan to turn out-of-balance green wood, buy mass. A lathe on a flimsy stand will shake no matter what its bed is made of.

A sliding or pivoting headstock lets you turn a larger bowl than the bed swing would otherwise allow. The JET 1440VS pivots 360 degrees to seven positions, and the Laguna Revo slides. These add flexibility for large work and outboard turning. Pivoting heads move the workpiece away from the bed, which gives you room to stand in front of a big bowl.

Most midi and full-size lathes use a 1 inch by 8 TPI spindle and a Morse taper tailstock. Check that chucks and faceplates are available. Budget separately for a chuck, live centre, tool rest and a set of gouges. Check that replacement belts, drive centres and tool rests are still sold for your model.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum diameter of the workpiece that clears the bed. Half of it is the distance from the spindle axis to the bed. Always compare with the bed length.
specDecoder.watchFor: A pivoting headstock allows more than the stated swing.

specDecoder.meaning: The longest workpiece that fits between the spindle and the tailstock. It matters most for long table legs.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 40 in on the JET 1640EVS suits long spindles, but the 20 in WEN is short.

specDecoder.meaning: Electronic variable speed uses a drive to change motor speed without belts. A VFD also allows soft starts.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Laguna uses a Delta S1 VFD with a TEFC motor.

specDecoder.meaning: A motor type with smooth torque and a wide speed range. It is sealed and quiet.
specDecoder.watchFor: The VEVOR 2HP lists it, but quality varies by maker.

specDecoder.meaning: The ability to spin the work in either direction, which helps with sanding. Hold the chuck by hand when reversing.
specDecoder.watchFor: Do not reverse with a threaded chuck unless it is locked.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared swing and bed length from 12 x 21 on the JET 1221VS to 18 x 40 on the VEVOR 2HP. We treated minimum speed as a safety feature.

howWeEvaluated.title: Speed range and control
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared minimum and maximum speeds, from 40 RPM on the JET 1640EVS to 400 RPM on the JET 1440VS, and noted electronic versus belt control. Cast iron mass was weighed against portability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor and mass
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at motor power from 6 amps to 2 HP and at cast iron versus lighter beds. Headstock flexibility was credited where stated.

howWeEvaluated.title: Headstock flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited sliding and pivoting headstocks for outboard and large bowl work. Motor torque was considered alongside horsepower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Evidence base
howWeEvaluated.description: This is based on spec sheets and owner feedback patterns, not our own bench time. Capacity numbers are manufacturer claims. Brand support was a tie-breaker.

howToChoose.subheading: Belt Drive vs Electronic Variable Speed

cards.label: Belt drive
cards.text: The JET 1221VS uses three belt ranges with variable speed in each. It is simple and durable but needs belt moves.

cards.label: Electronic variable
cards.text: The JET 1640EVS, Laguna Revo and VEVOR use electronic drives that change speed with a dial. They are more convenient and have better low-speed torque.

howToChoose.note: Choose electronic for large bowls and belt drive for simplicity.

howToChoose.subheading: For Large Green Bowl Blanks Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A low minimum speed, a heavy bed and a motor with torque at low RPM. Green blanks are unbalanced and heavy.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The JET 1640EVS starts at 40 RPM, the JET 1221VS at 60 and the Laguna Revo uses a VFD. The WEN 34035 at 250 RPM and the JET 1440VS at 400 are less suited.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You turn large bowls regularly. A heavy lathe with a low minimum speed is the safest.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You turn small bowls and spindles. The JET 1221VS or WEN 34035 does it.

maintenance.why: Rust and pitch stop the tailstock and banjo sliding. Use paste wax. Use paste wax.
A loose or cracked belt slips and loses torque. Replace if cracked.
Play or noise signals worn bearings. Spin by hand and feel for roughness.
Nicks in the rest make tool movement rough. Use fine abrasive on burrs.
Misalignment causes vibration and poor centring. Use a live centre as a test.

faq.q: What size lathe should I buy?
faq.a: Buy for the largest piece you will turn often. A midi like the JET 1221VS suits bowls to 10 inches, and a full-size lathe is needed for larger work. Buy tools after you know what you want to turn.

The WEN and VEVOR sit at the low end, the JET 1221VS and 1440VS in the middle and the JET 1640EVS and Laguna at the top. Pay more for mass and low-speed torque. Stands and benches matter as much as the lathe.
Many decades if the bed and bearings are good. Cast iron lathes are often handed down. Keep tools sharp, because dull tools cause more catches than any lathe fault.
Only if it holds torque at low speed. A 1 HP motor with good low-end torque beats a 2 HP motor that stalls. Lathes are often sold used, so inspect the spindle and bed.
For bowls, yes. A four-jaw chuck holds the blank securely and is the biggest accessory. A face shield is a better first purchase than extra accessories.
With a face shield, slow starts for rough blanks and correct tool rest height, yes. Never stand in line with a spinning blank. Start with small blanks until your technique is smooth.
